feeds.title: Edible Backyard Blog
feeds.description: I'm Kath Irvine. I've been growing all the vegetables to feed my family of 6 for 20 good years. Subscribe for your monthly shot of edible backyard inspiration! My seasonal tips, monthly calendar, and all the know how you need to keep your garden productive + healthy.

feeds.title: Kat's Garden Blog
feeds.description: In 2019, I moved with my partner to The Outpost, located in Te Hiku (Far North), New Zealand. We have 15ha, including over 5ha of native bush. My aim is to turn it into a thriving native ecosystem and food basket. At the moment, it is still mostly grass, however, we've planted hundreds of trees since we've been here. It'll take a few years to realize the goal, but we're well on the way.

feeds.title: Katrina Wolff
feeds.description: Read writing from Katrina Wolff. Katrina is a Compost Coach based in Titirangi, West Auckland, New Zealand. Using biodynamics to help home gardeners make top-quality soil.

feeds.title: Tikorangi The Jury Garden
feeds.description: Learn more about gardening tips, tricks, and information. Tikorangi is one of the few inter-generational, private gardens in New Zealand that has been intensively gardened through seven decades.

feeds.title: Organic Edible Garden Blog
feeds.description: Organic Edible Garden is a website with up-to-the-minute blog posts and videos on how to grow great-tasting vegetables and fruit in your own backyard.

feeds.title: Central Landscapes Blog
feeds.description: Follow Central Landscapes's gardening bog to learn about tips, tricks, and information to create a lively garden. Our Central Landscapes yards are franchised to local owners. We work together to give you the best landscaping products, available when you want them, seven days a week. We're passionate about landscape projects and healthy gardens, so we'll give you the best advice for your patch of paradise.

feeds.title: Zing Bokashi Blog
feeds.description: Zing Bokashi's easy to use range of home composting products will help you reduce and reuse waste, while naturally boosting the nutrients in your soil.

feeds.title: Canterbury Horticultural Society
feeds.description: Connecting people to the art, science, and practice of gardening and horticulture. New Zealand's largest gardening and the horticultural organisation providing information, garden tours and activities.

feeds.title: No Dig Garden Blog
feeds.description: Hi there, I'm Megan. I think I'm an addict as I get all jittery if I don't get my regular gardening fix. The idea to have this website came as a way to justify my earthy, dirty obsession with things that grow in the night... and day! Here you will find articles on how to grow vegetables by gardening without digging or tilling.

feeds.title: Studio Home Blog
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Julia. Inside spaces, outside spaces, and all the living and the creativity we find between them. Studio Home is my place to share ideas, inspiration, and art to help your home and garden feel like your own.

feeds.title: Fantail Valley Homestead
feeds.description: We help you learn to homestead, no matter where you live. Grow your own food and build your independence by joining our community, and become what your great grandparents would be proud of.

feeds.title: DIY Designs Blog
feeds.description: DIY Designs: An online landscape design company offering quality garden plans & landscape design services. Easy, achievable garden design ideas suitable for DIY.

feeds.title: Sarah The Gardener
feeds.description: Sarah O'Neil is an author, blogger and passionate gardener writing about the ups and downs of her country garden.

feeds.title: Good Magazine » Garden
feeds.description: The following section of Good Magazine is dedicated to gardening. Good is proudly New Zealand's leading and award-winning lifestyle and wellbeing publication for conscious consumers, driving positive conscience-living.

feeds.title: Kiwi Gardener
feeds.description: Kiwi Gardener is a magazine for gardeners who like to get their hands dirty. Our aim is to build on our connections with garden clubs and societies, continue to highlight the efforts of everyday Kiwi gardeners, and arms readers - especially beginners - with all they need to get the most out of their backyard, every season.

feeds.title: Home Grown Happiness » Garden
feeds.description: A collection of seasonal gardening advice for New Zealand gardens, plus no-dig gardening and organic gardening tips and tricks.
